name: Playlist Maker
description: Build playlists quickly with live genre/artist based recommendations, similar to Spotify or Apple Music.
overview: Adds a standalone Playlist Maker app (reachable by any user) with a fast search + drag-free playlist builder and a live 'more like this' recommendations panel, plus a Dashboard config page for Lidarr music requests and custom user requests.

versions.changelog:
## v1.1.9.0
- Request Music search boxes (artist and album) now show a "Searching…" indicator the moment a
  search starts, instead of leaving stale results/empty-state text visible with no feedback
  until the response arrives.
- Pressing Enter in either search box now runs the search immediately instead of waiting out the
  normal 300ms typing debounce.
- Fixed a race condition where typing quickly (or pressing Enter right after typing) could fire
  two overlapping searches, and a slower older response could land after a newer one and
  overwrite it with stale results - only the latest search's response is now ever applied.

## v1.1.8.0
- Add a favicon to the standalone app (/PlaylistMaker/App) so its browser tab shows a distinct
  icon instead of the browser's generic globe placeholder.
- Add server-log diagnostics for artist search results: since users keep reporting missing
  artist images even after the fallback fix (while album images work fine), Playlist Maker now
  logs, per search, how many Lidarr results actually had RemotePoster/Images data at all and
  which cover types were present. This will show definitively whether Lidarr itself isn't
  sending artist image data for these results, or whether something is actually being missed on
  this side - reproduce the missing-images search and check the Jellyfin server log for a line
  starting "Lidarr artist search for" to see which.

## v1.1.7.0
- Request an Artist no longer hides artists you already own part of the catalog for - they now
  show up with an "In your library" tag, so you can still find and browse them for albums
  you're missing. The plain album-title search still excludes owned albums as before.
- The per-artist "Show Albums" list now shows every album/single, including ones already in
  your library - those get a "In Library" checkmark instead of a Request button, so you can see
  the full picture of what you have vs. what's missing.
- Investigated the missing artist images further against Lidarr's own source: the resolution
  logic for artist and album images is structurally identical end to end, so this isn't a code
  bug - artist "fan art" coverage from Lidarr's metadata source is genuinely much sparser than
  album cover art coverage (which is close to universal). Results with no image at all now show
  a music-note placeholder instead of a blank box, so it's clearer that's what's happening
  rather than looking broken.

## v1.1.6.0
- Request an Artist now lets you browse and request individual albums/singles from that
  artist's catalog ("Show Albums"), instead of only being able to request their entire
  discography. Requesting the whole artist is still available as a separate button.
- Add custom requests: a link + optional note field in Request Music for anything the Lidarr
  artist/album search can't resolve on its own (a live recording, a bootleg, a rip from
  somewhere else, etc.), stored for an admin to review. Shares the same per-user rate limit as
  artist/album requests.
- The Dashboard config page (Dashboard > Plugins > Playlist Maker) no longer duplicates the
  standalone app's playlist builder - it's now just Lidarr settings plus the new Custom
  Requests review list, renamed to "Playlist Maker: Music Requests" to match. The standalone
  app at /PlaylistMaker/App is unaffected and remains the actual playlist builder.

## v1.1.5.0
- Fix: requesting an album never actually triggered a search in Lidarr. Lidarr's own add-album
  endpoint never refreshes the newly-created artist for a brand-new artist+album request, so the
  "search on add" flags (searchForNewAlbum / searchForMissingAlbums) never fired - they both only
  take effect once that refresh completes, which never happened. Now triggers a direct AlbumSearch
  command against the album right after it's added instead, which doesn't depend on that refresh.
- Both Request an Artist and Request an Album now leave out anything already in your library, so
  already-owned artists/albums don't show up as request-able.
- "Request an Album" now appears first in the Request Music panel, ahead of "Request an Artist".

## v1.1.4.0
- Add "Request an Album": search by album/single title and request just that release, instead
  of an artist's whole discography. The artist is added with monitoring scoped to only that one
  album (searched for immediately), since indexers distribute music album-by-album or as
  singles, never as a complete discography in one grab. Sits alongside the existing artist
  search in the Request Music panel.
- Artist photos in Request Music still weren't showing up for every result even after v1.1.3.0's
  fallback fix - many search results genuinely have no artist image cataloged by Lidarr's
  metadata source at all (this is sparse for less well-known artists); no further fix possible
  on the plugin side for those specific results.

## v1.1.3.0
- Fix: artist photos often didn't show up in Request Music search results, since Lidarr only
  fills in its "poster" image for artists that have one - many not-yet-added artists don't.
  Now falls back through cover, fanart, banner, and other available image types instead of
  leaving the row blank.
- Genre/artist chip search is now punctuation-insensitive: "sams", "sam's", and "sams'" all
  match the same chip, instead of an apostrophe or other punctuation blocking the match.
- Genre and artist chips have moved out of Search into their own "Browse by Genre & Artist"
  section, each with its own filter box to find a tag quickly in a large library.
- Picking a genre or artist chip now gives Recommended For You a deliberate mix instead of a
  plain ranked list: about 60% tracks that directly match the pick, 20% "adjacent" tracks
  (genres/artists that frequently show up alongside it in your library), and 20% wildcard
  tracks for discovery.
- Add an admin setting for the maximum number of music requests a user can make within a
  configurable time window (hours), to prevent one user from flooding Lidarr with requests.
  Off (unlimited) by default.
- Renamed the "Discover" panel/heading to "Search" for clarity.

## v1.1.2.0
- Fix: renaming an existing playlist while editing it didn't actually save - the "Update
  Playlist" save path only ever added/removed tracks, it never sent the name anywhere. Renaming
  now works, saved along with any track changes in the same update.

## v1.1.1.0
- Fix: searching was very slow (and could time out with no results) because genre matching
  pulled every track in the library into memory on every keystroke to check each one's genres
  by hand. Genre matching now uses the same indexed lookup the album match already used (search
  the genre entities by name, then filter tracks by id), which is how Jellyfin's own search
  stays fast at any library size.

## v1.1.0.0
- Add "Request Music": search Lidarr and request an artist be added to the library, directly
  from the standalone app - the same self-service pattern as Jellyseerr/Overseerr for movies
  and shows, but talking to Lidarr directly. An admin connects Lidarr from the Dashboard config
  page (URL, API key, root folder, quality/metadata profile); once configured, all users get a
  "Request Music" search box. Off by default until an admin sets it up.

## v1.0.9.0
- Fix: the "Your Playlist" playlist picker's open dropdown list was rendered by the browser
  itself (not the page), so it showed up in a plain white/black browser default style no matter
  what the rest of the app looked like - most browsers ignore page CSS for a native `<select>`'s
  open popup. Replaced it with a custom dropdown that's fully themed like the rest of the app.

## v1.0.8.0
- Add a persistent "now playing" bar at the bottom of the page while a preview is playing, with
  a seekable progress bar, play/pause, and a stop button - not just click-to-toggle on the cover.
- Fix: typing a genre name into search (e.g. "rock") found nothing, since search only matched
  track and album names. It now also matches genres, the same way picking a genre chip does.
- Fix: secondary text (album/artist line under each track, subtitles, hints, labels) was too dim
  to read comfortably - it relied on CSS opacity over a dark background, which crushes contrast
  further. Replaced with a fixed lighter gray so it's actually legible.

## v1.0.7.0
- Add click-to-preview: click a track's cover art anywhere (Discover, Recommended, Your
  Playlist) to play/pause a preview, like clicking a track in Spotify.
- Fix: some libraries have genre tags with multiple genres jammed into one string (bad NFO/scan
  metadata, e.g. "Rock, Folk, Live/1998"), which showed up as one long unreadable chip. Genre
  tags are now split apart, and genre/artist chip lists are collapsed to a compact default
  ("+N more" to expand) instead of dumping the whole library's tags as a wall of chips.
- Recommended For You refresh is a bigger change now: instead of a small random reorder of the
  same deterministic top matches, it draws from a much wider pool of good candidates and
  shuffles that pool, on top of already steering away from whatever was just shown.

## v1.0.6.0
- Fix: search only matched a track's own name, so searching for an album title found nothing.
  Now also matches albums by name and includes their tracks.
- Fix: picking a genre/artist chip only ever affected Recommended For You - Discover itself
  never changed, even though the empty-state text told you to "pick a genre / artist to get
  started." Chips now browse Discover directly when the search box is empty.
- Fix: refreshing Recommended For You tended to show mostly the same tracks, since scoring is
  deterministic and only had a small random jitter. Refreshing now steers away from whatever was
  just shown (falling back to the normal results if that leaves too few candidates), so hitting
  refresh actually surfaces different tracks.
- Quick Connect is now the default tab on sign-in when the server has it enabled, rather than
  requiring an extra click past the password form.
- Colors and font now match Jellyfin's own default dark theme exactly (background/card colors,
  accent blue, Noto Sans, button corner radius), pulled directly from jellyfin-web's theme
  source rather than approximated.

## v1.0.5.0
- Fix: a long, unbroken genre/artist tag (e.g. bad library metadata jammed into one tag) could
  force the whole page wider than the viewport instead of wrapping, since grid/flex items don't
  shrink below their content's natural width by default. Chips now truncate with an ellipsis
  (full text on hover) and the layout no longer blows out horizontally.
- Add Quick Connect as a sign-in option alongside username/password, for users who authenticate
  via SSO/OAuth and have no local Jellyfin password. Only shown if Quick Connect is enabled on
  the server.
- Add support for loading one of your existing playlists into the builder to edit it: add or
  remove tracks and save changes back, instead of only ever creating new playlists.
- Add a cover art uploader for playlists (available once a playlist has been created or loaded
  for editing). Jellyfin's own image endpoint is admin-only for any item; this adds an
  owner/editor-scoped upload path instead.
- Add track cover art (album art, falling back to the track's own embedded art) to every track
  row across Discover, Recommended For You, and Your Playlist.
- Fix: duplicate library entries of the same song (e.g. an album imported twice) could each show
  up separately in search and recommendations, and adding one copy to a playlist wouldn't stop
  the other copies from still being "recommended". Duplicate entries are now collapsed to one
  per song everywhere, and excluding a track now excludes every duplicate of that same song too.

## v1.0.4.0
- Fix (for real this time): every API call (Search/Genres/Artists/Recommendations) still
  failed with a 500 TypeLoadException/MissingMethodException on Jellyfin.Data.Entities.User
  even after v1.0.3.0. The actual cause was never a duplicate bundled assembly (the packaged
  plugin zip only ever contained this plugin's own DLL) - Jellyfin 10.11.x moved its host
  process from .NET 8 to .NET 9, so a plugin compiled for net8.0 was being loaded into a
  .NET 9 process, a genuine runtime ABI break. Now targets net9.0 and Jellyfin.Controller
  10.11.* to match the 10.11.x server line.

## v1.0.3.0
- Fix: every API call (Search/Genres/Artists/Recommendations) failed with a 500 error -
  TypeLoadException/MissingMethodException on Jellyfin.Data.Entities.User. `dotnet publish`
  was copying Jellyfin's own assemblies (Jellyfin.Data.dll, MediaBrowser.Controller.dll, etc.)
  into this plugin's own output folder. The server ended up with two different copies of those
  assemblies loaded at once - its own, and this plugin's bundled copy - and the CLR treats
  identically-named types from two different assembly instances as unrelated types. Excluded
  those packages' runtime assets from the build so only the host's own copies are ever used.

## v1.0.2.0
- Add a standalone app at /PlaylistMaker/App with its own login screen, reachable by any user
  (not just admins). Jellyfin's web client wraps its entire Dashboard section - where every
  plugin's config page lives, including this one - in an admin-only route guard, so the
  Dashboard page could never be reached by regular users no matter what else was fixed. This
  new page is served directly by the plugin, completely outside jellyfin-web's app shell, and
  authenticates with a normal Jellyfin username/password.

## v1.0.1.0
- Fix: the page rendered completely unstyled and never loaded any data. Jellyfin's page loader
  only keeps markup that lives inside the page's root `data-role="page"` div and discards
  everything else, so the separate playlistmaker.js/.css files were silently dropped on load.
  Everything is now a single self-contained page (inline styles + script), matching the pattern
  Jellyfin's own bundled plugins use.
- Fix: track fields from the API (Name, Id, Artists, etc.) are PascalCase; the UI was reading
  camelCase names and rendering nothing as a result.

  and build a playlist.
- Live "Recommended For You" panel that scores your library by genre/artist overlap with the
  current draft.
- Cold-start fallback surfaces popular/recently added tracks when nothing has been picked yet.

  tracks for discovery.

## v1.1.2.0

  stays fast at any library size.
